Excel compatibility

DocCells reads and writes the Excel .xlsx format. The following is kept, both ways.

What is kept

ItemRemark
values, texts, dates, formulasformulas are displayed in DocCells' language
number formatsincluding custom ones
font, colors, alignment, rotation, wrapping
borders, merged cells
widths, heights, hidden rows and columns
frozen rows and columns, gridlines
several sheets
named ranges
conditional formattingDocCells' rules, Excel's simple rules (comparison, text contained)
checkboxes, drop-down lists
chartswritten as Excel charts; DocCells' are read back
images
filters
protection, unlocked cells

What is not

ItemBecomes
linkstheir text
lists in cellsa text, [2, 1]
sparklines of DocCells or Google Sheetsa SPARKLINE formula, read back by DocCells; unknown to Excel
charts created in Excelnot kept
pivot tables, macros, slicers, commentsnot kept
conditional formatting with color scales, bars, iconsnot kept

Before replacing a complex Excel workbook, save it from DocCells under another name (Save as...).

Lists

A list reopened from an .xlsx is a text: typing it again makes it a list. A list calculated by a formula is a list again when the formula is recalculated.

Formulas

On opening, a formula generally keeps the result saved by Excel until one of its cells changes. A function not computed by DocCells then gives #NAME? or #ERROR!.

Other formats

FormatHow
.csvopen the file in a text editor, copy, paste in DocCells if the values are separated by tabs; otherwise, convert it to .xlsx
.ods, .xlssave them as .xlsx with LibreOffice or Excel
Google Sheetsby its link, or downloaded as .xlsx
PDFprint, “Save as PDF”
